steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: US independent film is produced outside the major Hollywood studio system, typically with lower budgets, creative freedom and alternative approaches to narrative, representation and style.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Independent filmmaking often prioritises personal vision, artistic experimentation and social relevance over commercial considerations and mass audience appeal.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Key indie aesthetics include naturalistic performance, location shooting, handheld cinematography, non-linear narratives and ambiguous endings that challenge mainstream conventions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Sundance Film Festival, founded by Robert Redford in 1978, became the premier showcase for American independent film and a launchpad for indie careers and distribution.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When comparing indie and mainstream, identify specific differences in narrative, representation, aesthetics and ideology — not just budget. Use concrete examples from your set film to illustrate indie characteristics rather than discussing them abstractly. Acknowledge that the indie-mainstream boundary is blurred and that your set film may contain elements of both. Consider how the film's independent production context shaped the choices the filmmaker was able to make. Discuss the limitations as well as the freedoms of independent filmmaking — budget constraints affect every creative decision.
